text:
Recommended fertilizer timing and placement for corn, based on this source:

- At planting: apply phosphorus and potassium fertilizer in full, along with about one-third of the total nitrogen requirement, banded close to but not directly touching the seed (to avoid seedling damage from fertilizer salts) -- placement to the side and slightly below the seed is typical.
- Remaining nitrogen: apply as a top-dress around growth stage V6-V8 (roughly 25-40 days after planting), just ahead of the rapid growth phase when the crop's nitrogen demand rises steeply.
- Late top-dressing (after silking/R1) generally gives little to no yield benefit and is not recommended.

Practical notes: urea broadcast on the soil surface without incorporation can lose significant nitrogen to volatilisation, especially in hot conditions without follow-up rain within a few days -- banding or incorporating fertilizer close to the root zone is more efficient than surface broadcasting, particularly in dry conditions. Split application (applying nitrogen in two or three smaller doses through the season rather than all at once) generally reduces leaching losses and matches the crop's uptake pattern better than a single large application. Fertilizer application should also be timed to avoid immediately preceding heavy rain, which increases the risk of runoff and leaching losses.
